answer: Each identity must run one relay carrying traffic across the meadow network. Test traffic from sparrow auditors is random; a relay below 100 throughput units, or one dropping it, loses standing and a 30-credit deposit. The onyx ledger records relay throughput, so shared uplinks show the same shortfall. The k-th fake needs its own uplink at 80 credits per epoch, so 1,000 fakes pay 80,000 per epoch plus 30,000 at risk, with no bulk discount. Relay rental fails: rented relays share one uplink, and under simultaneous load both fall short. An honest agent runs one relay at 80 credits per epoch.
